settings_help.source: (str) - Where Mask Generation keeps the fields Measure reads. 'ome-zarr' writes each field straight into fov.ome.zarr in the project folder: preprocessing stores the acquired channels there (no stack/ folder), and the masks are added as label images; one OME-Zarr plate store (row/column/field), the channels in their acquired dtype, one shard file per field image and per label image; no merged/*.npy is written. 'npy' writes stack/*.npy and merged/*.npy as before. 'tiff' writes merged/*.npy plus merged_tiff/<field>.tif and <field>_<object>_mask.tif. A timelapse field is ONE field with a time axis (t, c, y, x; its masks t, y, x), every frame still read by its own field name; z slices are stored as acquired on a z axis and the maximum projection Mask segments and Measure measures is computed when the field is read. Older projects with stack/, merged/*.npy or images/<plate>.ome.zarr still read. Default 'ome-zarr'. Alpha.

(bool) - Keep the run's working masks/ folders after every field is merged. Off by default: they are removed once each field is committed to fov.ome.zarr (or merged/ for 'npy' runs), which holds the channels and every mask. With fov.ome.zarr no stack/ folder is written at all: preprocessing stores each field's channels straight into fov.ome.zarr. Older projects' stack/ folders are still read, and kept or removed by this setting as before.

(bool) - What happens to the original image files once their pixels are in fov.ome.zarr. On (the default): after each field is committed to fov.ome.zarr and every channel plane is verified byte for byte against its original, that field's originals are moved into orig/ in the project folder. Off: each original is deleted, but only after that same check passed for its field; this saves the disk space of a second copy and cannot be undone. z slices are stored as acquired, so each slice file is compared with its own stored plane; only a field whose channels had different z slices (stored as their maximum projection) has no single plane to compare, so its originals are moved to orig/ even when this is off. A run cut short never loses an image: the next run checks again and finishes the moves or deletions. With mask_image_format 'npy' or 'tiff', the originals go to orig/ and are deleted at the end only when this is off, as before. save_original_images off or delete_intermediate on also turn keeping off. Default True.

(bool) - The older switch for the original images. Off acts as keep_original_images off: with fov.ome.zarr each original is deleted only after its field is committed and verified there; with 'npy' or 'tiff' runs the raw images are deleted once they are in stack/, as before, which is not reversible. Use keep_original_images instead. Default True.

(bool) - When True, spaCR requires the array to contain an explicit z dimension and raises an error instead of inferring the axis; this enables z_segmentation_mode, anisotropy and stitch_threshold. Standard ingestion stores every z slice in fov.ome.zarr and segments its maximum-intensity projection, computed on read, so it segments in 2-D; supply volumetric arrays directly to spacr.zstack instead. When False, no z-stack code runs and masks match a two-dimensional run. Default False.
